description: The original aircraft that made the first east-to-west aeroplane crossing of the North Atlantic on 12-13 April 1928 flown by Hermann Köhl, Günther von Hünefeld and James Fitzmaurice. Bought by Henry Ford after the flight and kept at Dearborn for decades; on long-term loan from the Henry Ford Museum and displayed in the Bremenhalle since 2009.

Focke-Wulf Fw 44 Stieglitz trainer biplane, a type designed and built in Bremen by Focke-Wulf under Kurt Tank, displayed in the Bremenhalle beside the Junkers W 33. Registration not established from the sources consulted.

Spacelab module, the reusable laboratory flown in the Space Shuttle cargo bay and developed largely by the Bremen space company ERNO; exhibited in the Bremenhalle as part of the Bremen aerospace history display.
